state: committed and verified in CI on the pull request head; not observed on a deployed brain
evidence_kind: real Postgres principals and schemas in CI; mocked Redis, docker and compose

runs.red_note: Each red run is a dispatched diffcheck of the red test commit with the earlier failing seam's test removed, because a failing pytest step stops the later service steps.

measurement.brain_backend_scope_conflicts: Counter per kind (vault, principal, schema, redis, backup) in agentibrain.backends, printed by the CLI as brain_backend_scope_conflicts kind=<k> count=<n>; embeddings logs the same line on refusal; brain-api and brain-ops refuse with the owning brain named

interfaces: agentibrain.backends: BackendBinding.from_settings, scope_conflicts, installed_conflicts, claim_vault, backup_vault, restore_vault, namespaced, BackendScopeError
agentibrain up and install refuse shared backends before compose starts and claim the vault
run_migrations passes brain_id to psql and reports a database held by another brain; up and install exit 1 on it
migration 004_brain_instance and embeddings init.sql: one row brain_instance claim
embeddings get_pool refuses a foreign schema claim or a principal that can read another brain's claim
brain-ops instance_scope: namespaced keys, claim_vault, claim_stream; used by brain_tick, amygdala and tick_cycle
compatibility: An unnamed brain keeps the legacy Redis keys and stream names and claims its vault, schema and stream as default on first start; no migration. The brain-ops chart no longer pins EVENT_BUS_STREAM, so a named brain's stream follows its BRAIN_ID.
rollback: Stop only the misconfigured brain and restore its previous BRAIN_ID, POSTGRES_URL, REDIS_URL and vault. Claims are authoritative ownership state and are not deleted to pass a refusal. Rehearsed in CI by the misbinding fixtures; not rehearsed on a deployed brain.
limitations: Vault restore is a library function, agentibrain.backends.restore_vault, with no CLI command yet
Services log or raise on conflicts; only the CLI keeps an in-process counter
installed_conflicts sees only brains installed on the same host; cross host misbinding is caught by the vault, schema and stream claims at startup
Compose stacks keep the legacy AMYGDALA_STREAMS default; a named brain on a shared external Redis is refused by the stream claim rather than namespaced
The brain-ops scope claim code is duplicated in brain-api because neither image ships the agentibrain package
